newsitem.title: CHINA: Shenzhen B shares end lower on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B shares end lower on profit-taking.

text.p: Shenzhen's hard currency B share index ended lower on Tuesday, driven down by profit-taking after a rebound in the past three sessions, brokers said.
The index lost 1.44 points or 1.07 percent to 132.81 points on turnover of HK$56 million, down from Monday's HK$73 million.

The domestic A share index recovered early losses to end up 2.21 points or 0.54 percent at 413.23 points due to heavy selective buying of comapnies expected to report healthy 1997 interim earnings, brokers said.
Turnover in the A share market was 7.0 billion yuan against 7.8 billion yuan on Monday.
"Foreign institutional investors were seen cashing in on the B share market's recent gains," an analyst at J&A Securities (HK) Ltd said.
"B share turnover remained thin, showing cautious sentiment," the analyst said.

Slight optimism, mixed with some caution over listed firms' first-half 1997 earnings, was likely to make both the A and B share indices a bit volatile in the early stages of China's interim reporting season, brokers said.
China's corporate interim reporting season started at the beginning of July and ends on August 31.
"Trading in the two markets should be marked by active selective buying of stocks expected to post good interim earnings and dumping of bad shares," an analyst at China Guotai Securities said.
In the B share market, newcomer Bengang Steel Plates was the most actively traded issue on volume of 2.82 million shares, losing HK$0.03 to HK$2.21.
Chengming Paper, hurt by institutional profit-taking, dipped HK$0.27 to HK$7.43, brokers said.
Volume reached 2.17 million shares, making it the second most actively traded B stock.
Brokers said the A share market advance was helped in part by the recent slowdown in market expansion, which had resulted in less funds being diverted from listed shares.

Beijing had been slowing market expansion since the beginning of this month on the belief that a string of anti-speculation measures launched in May and June had effectively cooled the markets, brokers said.
Recently-listed Huludao Zinc, China's biggest zinc smelter, rose 0.66 yuan to 11.67 yuan on volume of 18 million shares, making it the most actively traded A share.
